subject: Dedicated reservation offer — cluster sizing & ramp for NovusMinds
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@novusminds.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@novusminds.ai>, Leah Rivers <leah.r@novusminds.ai>

Subject: Dedicated capacity options — sizing question

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We liked Redwood's performance profile but need to lock down several commercial knobs before we can take this to procurement: cluster size minimum, how quickly we can ramp from pilot to full production, and fallback/burst behavior if demand spikes.

Key asks from our side:
- Minimum guaranteed GPUs vs. practical baseline for latency-sensitive inference (we're serving low-latency chat and real-time reranking).
- Typical ramp cadence (weeks to move from 10 GPUs to 100 GPUs) and any warm-start credits.
- How burst capacity is priced and whether there are pre-warmed lanes to avoid cold starts.

Can you send a couple of reservation options (including cost buckets) and a recommended ramp schedule that we can present to procurement next week?

Also copying Leah (ops) and procurement for visibility.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of ML Infrastructure, NovusMinds
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@novusminds.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 23 May 2028 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity options — sizing question

Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short options pack (NovusMinds_Reserve_Options_v1.pdf) plus a cost workbook (novus_cost_model_v1.xlsx). Summary here so you have something concise for procurement:

Option A — Pilot-to-Scale (Conservative)
- Cluster baseline: 12 GPUs (4x A100-80GB equivalents)
- Minimum committed floor: 12 GPUs (keeps warm KV cache active per tenant)
- Ramp plan: 12 → 40 GPUs over 6 weeks (triggered by usage milestones)
- Burst: additional on-demand pool billed at spot/overage rate; optional hot-lane (pre-warmed) for predictable bursts (extra monthly fee)
- SLA target: 99.5% availability on committed floor
- Best for: teams that want low upfront commit and fast fall-back to on-demand

Option B — Anchored Growth (Balanced)
- Cluster baseline: 48 GPUs (16x A100-80GB equivalents)
- Minimum committed floor: 24 GPUs (reduces per-token cost via batching)
- Ramp plan: 24 → 48 GPUs over 8–10 weeks with predefined activation windows every 2 weeks
- Burst: 20% burst buffer included in the reserved pool during predictable peaks
- Warm-start credits: 40 GPU-hours for initial activation windows to limit cold-start billing
- SLA target: 99.7% availability on committed floor
- Best for: teams with steady growth forecasts and tighter unit-cost targets

Option C — Performance Anchor (Aggressive)
- Cluster baseline: 160 GPUs (high-throughput lane)
- Minimum committed floor: 80 GPUs
- Ramp plan: staged: 80 → 120 (month 1) → 160 (month 3) with canary pre-warm stages
- Burst: large reserved surge lanes with automatic fallback to smaller variants if capacity constrained
- Warm-start credits: 200 GPU-hours and priority scheduling for pre-warm windows
- SLA target: 99.9% availability on committed floor; priority routing across regions
- Best for: real-time, low-latency product where cost-of-outage is high

Tradeoffs and notes:
- Minimum floor keeps KV caches hot and reduces per-token latency — lowering baseline increases cold-start risk and per-token cost.
- We can pre-commit burst lanes (hot-lane) if you have predictable daily/weekly peaks — that smooths latency at higher cost.
- Billing: committed floor billed monthly; ramp activations prorated within the month. Overage/burst at published spot/overage rates; we can build a blended committed+burst rate in the workbook if you prefer.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Decide which option maps to your initial org risk tolerance (A/B/C).
2) Share preferred ramp dates so we can lock activation windows into our capacity calendar.
3) If procurement needs an alternative pricing line (e.g., 12-month vs 36-month commit), we can produce a short paper with blended unit economics.

I've looped Ben and Marcus on technical/ops caveats — Ben can comment on warm-start mechanics and Marcus can provide a refined cost delta for different GPU models.

Attaching: NovusMinds_Reserve_Options_v1.pdf (proposal brief), novus_cost_model_v1.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 May 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity options — sizing question (internal notes)

Jasmine / Marcus — quick internal thread with suggested tweaks before I send the annotated file back to Samir.

Notes:
- For Option A: recommend adding a 6-hour daily pre-warm (windowed) instead of 40 GPU-hours lump sum — easier for ops to schedule and aligns with their peak times (they mentioned US mornings).
- For Option B: reduce the minimum committed floor to 20 GPUs for the first 90 days and auto-evaluate at day 90 — that gives NovusMinds a softer entry while still preserving batching benefits.
- For Option C: propose a canary lane (8 GPUs) that mirrors production model weights to validate before each major activation — reduces risk of regressions during ramp.

I've attached a marked-up PDF and a short note to include in the procurement packet explaining the canary and pre-warm mechanics. Marcus, can you update the workbook with the 20 GPU transitional floor and the alternate pricing for 24 vs 20 floor?

Ben
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
